###### November 9, 2026


*Adds four commercial-stage products — ZYNRELEF®, APONVIE®, CINVANTI® and SUSTOL® — to CorMedix’s hospital- and acute-care-focused commercial platform*


*Upfront consideration consisting of $145 million in cash, subject to customary purchase price adjustments, plus 14,583,333 shares of CorMedix common stock*


*Additional consideration of up to $55 million in earn-out payments to Heron tied to calendar year 2028 ZYNRELEF net sales plus a royalty on net sales of certain products above a sales threshold*


*Transaction expected to be immediately accretive to CorMedix earnings and free cash flow, as well as estimated to generate $45-$60 million in near-term total operating cost synergies*


*CorMedix entered into a new senior secured term loan facility with funds managed by Pharmakon Advisors and will draw $75 million of non-dilutive financing to support the transaction*


*Heron to remain a publicly traded company with its credit facility repaid, a significant position in CorMedix common stock and rights to earn-out and royalty payments*


*Transaction expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, subject to regulatory clearance and approval by Heron stockholders and other customary closing conditions*


*CorMedix to host a conference call and webcast today at 4:30 p.m. Eastern Time*


**PARSIPPANY, N.J. and CARY, N.C., November 9, 2026** — CorMedix Therapeutics (Nasdaq: CRMD) (“CorMedix”) and Heron Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: HRTX) (“Heron”) today announced that they have entered into a definitive asset purchase agreement (the “Agreement”) under which CorMedix will acquire substantially all of the assets of Heron, and assume certain of Heron’s liabilities, for upfront consideration consisting of $145 million in cash, subject to customary purchase price adjustments, plus 14,583,333 shares of CorMedix common stock, plus up to $55 million in contingent earn-out payments and royalties on net sales of certain Heron products. The transaction has been unanimously approved by the Boards of Directors of both companies.


The acquisition adds four commercial-stage products to CorMedix’s portfolio: ZYNRELEF (bupivacaine and meloxicam) extended-release solution for postoperative pain; APONVIE (aprepitant) injectable emulsion for the prevention of postoperative nausea and vomiting; CINVANTI (aprepitant) injectable emulsion and SUSTOL (granisetron) extended-release injection for the prevention of chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting. Each is administered in hospitals, ambulatory surgical centers or infusion centers — the institutional settings of care where CorMedix has built its commercial infrastructure. The transaction also includes the assumption of Heron’s rights with respect to products covered by Heron’s multi-product Development and License Agreement.


**Management Commentary**


“This acquisition is a meaningful step forward in our strategy to build a diversified portfolio of products used in institutional settings of care, which creates substantial value for CorMedix shareholders,” said Joseph Todisco, Chairman & Chief Executive Officer of CorMedix. “Heron’s products are a natural fit for the commercial platform we have built, and we see ZYNRELEF in particular as an asset with significant untapped potential as hospitals and surgery centers increasingly adopt non-opioid approaches to postsurgical pain. We expect to realize $45-$60 million in operating cost synergies by leveraging our existing infrastructure, and we have structured this transaction in a manner which will be immediately accretive to earnings and free cash flow. Importantly, the Pharmakon facility gives us an efficient source of non-dilutive capital to fund this transaction while preserving dry powder for additional growth-oriented business development opportunities, including the flexibility of a second $75 million tranche to fund further growth.”


“Following a thorough review of strategic alternatives, our Board concluded that this transaction offers the most compelling path forward for Heron stockholders,” said Craig Collard, Chief Executive Officer of Heron. “The transaction provides substantial consideration through a combination of cash, CorMedix stock and earn-out payments, enabling Heron to complete the repayment of its outstanding credit facility with Hercules and become a significant stockholder of a company we believe is well-positioned for future growth and value creation. In addition, the earn-out and royalties provide the opportunity for Heron and our stockholders to further benefit from the success of the products our team has built. I am deeply grateful to the entire Heron team for their hard work advancing the standard of care for patients, and I believe that CorMedix has the scale, financial strength and institutional commercial focus to accelerate the growth of ZYNRELEF and APONVIE and to help ensure that CINVANTI continues to reach the patients who rely on it.”


**Transaction Terms**


Under the terms of the Agreement, CorMedix will pay upfront consideration consisting of $145 million in cash, subject to customary purchase price adjustments, and issue 14,583,333 shares of CorMedix common stock. The number of shares was determined by dividing $105 million by $7.20 per share and is fixed, subject to customary adjustment for stock splits and similar events; it will not be adjusted for changes in CorMedix’s share price prior to closing. Based on the closing price of CorMedix common stock of $5.32 on November 6, 2026, the stock consideration has a value of approximately $77.6 million, and the upfront consideration has an aggregate value of approximately $222.6 million.


In addition to the upfront consideration, Heron will be eligible to receive:


- **Total earn-out payments of up to $55 million** : $25 million if ZYNRELEF net sales equal or exceed $65 million for calendar year 2028, plus an additional $30 million if ZYNRELEF net sales equal or exceed $95 million for calendar year 2028; and
- **A 5% royalty on the portion of combined annual net sales** of CINVANTI, SUSTOL and the products covered by Heron’s multi-product Development and License Agreement which exceed $25 million in calendar year 2027, calendar year 2028 and calendar year 2029.


In connection with the transaction, Rubric Capital Management LP (“Rubric”), the holder of Heron’s senior unsecured convertible notes due 2031, has agreed to exchange this debt, consisting of $35.0 million in aggregate principal amount of such notes plus accrued and unpaid interest (approximately $37.8 million in the aggregate as of September 30, 2026), for shares of CorMedix common stock received by Heron (the “Exchange”). This Exchange between Heron and Rubric is expected to occur in four quarterly tranches following the closing, subject to the terms and conditions of the exchange agreement.


Both Heron and Rubric have entered into respective governance agreements with CorMedix, wherein Heron shall have the right to name one new member to the CorMedix Board of Directors for so long as Heron continues to hold at least 10% of the outstanding shares of CorMedix and where each of Heron and Rubric have agreed to prohibitions on certain conduct and limitations on trading in CorMedix shares.


The transaction is subject to approval by Heron stockholders, the expiration or termination of the applicable waiting period under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act of 1976, and other customary closing conditions. The transaction is not subject to any financing contingency and is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027.


In connection with the transaction, certain Heron stockholders holding approximately 22% of Heron’s outstanding common stock, including Rubric, have entered into voting agreements with Heron and CorMedix pursuant to which they have agreed to vote their shares in favor of the transaction.


**Strategic Rationale**


The acquisition advances CorMedix’s strategy of expanding its portfolio with differentiated products used in institutional settings of care. Following its acquisition of Melinta Therapeutics, CorMedix has assembled a commercial organization focused on hospitals, infusion centers, dialysis clinics and other institutional settings of care. The Heron portfolio is highly complementary to this footprint, sharing overlapping call points across hospital pharmacy and therapeutics committees, group purchasing organizations, integrated delivery networks and ambulatory surgical centers.


- **Scale and diversification:** Adds an established revenue base of approximately $150 million on September 30, 2026, trailing twelve-month net product revenue across acute care and oncology supportive care, further broadening CorMedix’s revenue mix.
- **Commercial and operational leverage:** Deploys Heron’s products through CorMedix’s existing institutional commercial, market access, medical affairs and supply chain infrastructure, driving the $45–$60 million in total expected operating cost synergies.
- **Growth from the acute care franchise:** ZYNRELEF and APONVIE represent the fastest-growing products in the Heron portfolio and are positioned for continued expansion in the hospital and ambulatory surgical center settings.
- **Expanded hematology/oncology presence:** CINVANTI, SUSTOL and products covered by Heron’s multi-product Development and License Agreement complement CorMedix’s emerging position in the space with REZZAYO® (rezafungin for injection), which is currently indicated for treating candidemia and invasive candidiasis and in development for prophylaxis of invasive fungal disease in allogeneic stem cell transplant patients.


**Expected Pro Forma Financial Profile and Financing**\[1\]


CorMedix expects the transaction to be immediately accretive to earnings and free cash flow upon closing and to generate operating cost synergies of an estimated $45-$60 million on an annualized run-rate basis by year-end 2027, driven primarily by the elimination of redundant commercial, general and administrative, and public company expenses.


CorMedix expects pro forma 2026 estimated revenue for the combined business to be $465-$490 million. In addition, CorMedix expects the acquired Heron assets to generate approximately $125–150 million of estimated pro forma revenue in 2027.


Concurrent with the signing of the Agreement, CorMedix entered into a new $150 million senior secured term loan facility with funds managed by Pharmakon Advisors, LP (“Pharmakon”). Under the facility, CorMedix expects to draw $75 million at the closing of the Heron asset acquisition, and an additional $75 million tranche may be drawn at CorMedix’s discretion through June 30, 2028 to support future business development transactions.


Pharmakon Advisors, LP is a leading investor in non-dilutive debt for the life sciences industry and serves as the investment manager for the BioPharma Credit funds. Established in 2009, funds managed by Pharmakon Advisors have committed $12.9 billion across 82 investments.


Key terms of the asset purchase agreement with Heron, the loan facility and other agreements referenced herein will be described in a Current Report on Form 8-K to be filed by CorMedix with the Securities and Exchange Commission.


**Heron Commentary**


Following the closing, Heron will exit the operation of its current biotechnology business and other historical operations, but it does not intend to liquidate and will remain a publicly traded company. Heron will retain significant federal and state net operating loss carryforwards (approximately $2.3 billion as of September 30, 2026), certain other tax attributes and other material assets, including the shares of CorMedix common stock issued to Heron, the right to receive future royalties and earn-out payments, and cash on hand. Following the closing, the Heron Board of Directors intends to actively evaluate various strategic transactions and opportunities for the use of the proceeds of the transaction, including acquiring or investing in additional businesses or assets, which may or may not be pharmaceutical or biotechnology businesses or assets. Such opportunities may include, but are not limited to, the acquisition of products, product candidates, milestone payments and royalty streams, programs or technologies as well as pursuing strategic alliances, joint ventures, investments in complementary businesses, out-licensing and in-licensing agreements, divestitures or other transactions. It is currently uncertain what businesses or assets Heron may acquire or invest in following the closing of the transaction, and the Heron Board of Directors intends to evaluate opportunities to create value for the benefit of stockholders.


Key terms of the asset purchase agreement with CorMedix and other agreements referenced herein will be described in a Current Report on Form 8-K to be filed by Heron with the Securities and Exchange Commission.


**Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results**


CorMedix will report third quarter 2026 financial results on November 12, 2026. Please refer to CorMedix’s press release issued[here](https://cormedix.com/cormedix-therapeutics-to-report-third-quarter-2026-financial-results-and-provide-a-corporate-update-on-november-12-2026/) to register and for more information.


Heron reports its third quarter 2026 financial results today, November 9, 2026. In light of the transaction with CorMedix, Heron will not hold an associated conference call.

**About CorMedix**


CorMedix Therapeutics is a biopharmaceutical company focused on developing and commercializing therapeutic products for the prevention and treatment of life-threatening conditions and diseases in the United States. CorMedix is focused on selling and marketing products in institutional care settings in the U.S. and has field-based medical and commercial infrastructure deployed in hospitals, clinics and infusion centers. For more information visit:[www.cormedix.com](http://www.cormedix.com/) .


**About Heron Therapeutics**


Heron Therapeutics, Inc. is a commercial-stage biotechnology company focused on improving the lives of patients by developing and commercializing therapeutic innovations that improve medical care. Our advanced science, patented technologies, and innovative approach to drug discovery and development have allowed us to create and commercialize a portfolio of products that aim to advance the standard-of-care for acute care and oncology patients. For more information, visit[www.herontx.com](http://www.herontx.com/) .
